note: Editorial file. 'now' must be factual and sourced; 'meaning' is Procurement Signal's analysis. Refresh each newsroom run when the cost monitor or category news changes.

steel.now: Producer prices hit a new high in August, up 23.4% on the year. Importers also pay a 50% Section 232 duty on full customs value since April 6.
steel.meaning: Landed cost for imported steel is rising faster than the index shows. Suppliers have pricing power, so flat annual increases will lag the market.

aluminum.now: Prices are 5.9% below their June high but still 27.3% above a year ago. Imports carry a 50% Section 232 duty on full value.
aluminum.meaning: Contracts priced at spring highs are now above market. The pullback is a window to re-quote, but the duty keeps imported landed cost elevated.

copper.now: Copper and brass mill shapes are at a 12-month high, up 20.9% on the year. Copper and derivatives are covered by the April 2026 Section 232 metals proclamation.
copper.meaning: Wire, cable and copper-intensive component suppliers face higher input and duty costs. Expect pass-through requests and check which parts are copper-heavy.

resins.now: Plastic resin prices have fallen 8.5% over three months and are among the categories that turned lower this year.
resins.meaning: Input costs for packaging and molded-part suppliers are falling. Buyers have leverage to re-quote rather than accept increases set earlier in the year.

chemicals.now: Industrial chemical prices have eased over three months but remain 13.3% above a year ago.
chemicals.meaning: The direction has turned in buyers' favor. Before accepting increases, ask suppliers to show how lower input costs are reflected in their price.

diesel.now: Diesel jumped 17.7% in August after easing from a May peak and is up 77.8% on the year.
diesel.meaning: Volatility, not the base rate, is driving freight and delivered-price changes. Fuel surcharge tables in carrier and supplier contracts now matter more than the headline rate.

ocean.now: Deep-sea freight is up 32.0% on the year and near its 24-month high. Shippers are shifting volume to the Port of Los Angeles as Panama Canal constraints persist.
ocean.meaning: Routing changes add transit time and variability, so capacity and lead time are as much a risk as rate. Inventory buffers for ocean-dependent parts may need to grow.

sources.name: Supply Chain Dive: Panama Canal challenges drive shippers to Port of Los Angeles

trucking.now: Truck transportation prices have been flat for three months in the government data, while Cass reported truckload linehaul rates up 10% in September.
trucking.meaning: The official index lags the market. A September rise in linehaul rates suggests contract renewals will be tougher than the flat index implies.

sources.name: FreightWaves: Cass TL linehaul rates up 10% in September

semis.now: Semiconductors are the only tracked category below year-ago prices, down 3.1%. Section 232 tariffs on semiconductors are in effect.
semis.meaning: Supplier prices are softening even as duties apply to imports. Compare landed cost, not just quoted price, before renegotiating.

electrical.now: Electrical machinery and equipment prices are up 13.5% on the year. Some metal-intensive grid equipment carries a 15% Section 232 rate through 2027.
electrical.meaning: Metal costs and duties are both feeding into equipment pricing. Budget for landed cost above the index for imported electrical equipment.

lumber.now: Lumber prices are up 7.6% on the year, and Section 232 tariffs on wood products are in effect.
lumber.meaning: Pallet and crating costs follow lumber. Check how pallet and packaging suppliers price wood content in their contracts.

paper.now: Converted paper and paperboard, including corrugated boxes, is up 4.4% on the year but accelerating to a 12.9% annualized pace.
paper.meaning: Box pricing is turning up from a low base. Check when corrugated contracts reset before increases arrive.
